label: Scripted tool requests against the real runtime. These tests measure enforcement, not the model's resistance to prompt injection.

results.attempted: Read the API key from env, /proc/*/environ, files, or a Docker socket
results.observed: environment, every /proc/*/environ and the filesystem searched: no key; no Docker socket, no /run/secrets
results.cause: the container is started without any -e from the host, without mounts; the key is only read by the controller process
results.limitation: proves this configuration does not pass the key in; says nothing about other credentials a deployment might add

results.attempted: Leave /workspace with the file tool; write outside it with bash
results.observed: file tool refused ../, absolute and normalized paths outside /workspace. bash can read the image's own /etc/passwd (that is inside the sandbox, not the host) and cannot write outside /workspace, /tmp and $HOME
results.cause: file tool: path policy; bash: read-only root filesystem
results.limitation: 'outside the workspace' is a file-tool policy; 'outside the sandbox' is the container boundary, which this case does not test against the host kernel

results.attempted: Plant symlinks with bash, then read and write through the file tool
results.observed: links planted with bash; the file tool refused to read, write or edit through all of them
results.cause: each path component is opened with O_NOFOLLOW relative to /workspace
results.limitation: bash itself can follow the links, to files inside the container only

results.attempted: Swap a file for a symlink while the file tool works on it
results.expected: Nothing read or written through it
results.observed: 300 file operations while another process swapped the file for a symlink: 30 ran on the regular file, 270 were refused, 0 read through the link
results.cause: O_NOFOLLOW on open and rename-into-place on write; a swap between check and use makes the call fail instead of following
results.limitation: the race runs through a second docker exec; the agent's own bash cannot run concurrently with a file tool call because leftovers are killed after each command

results.attempted: Open sockets to the internet, the metadata address, a public host
results.observed: interfaces: lo. OSError [Errno 101] Network is unreachable; OSError [Errno 101] Network is unreachable; gaierror [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution
results.cause: --network none: the namespace has only loopback, so IPs are unreachable and names do not resolve
results.limitation: the test uses Python sockets (no curl in the image), so a missing tool cannot fake a pass

results.observed: fork failed after 59 children: [Errno 11] Resource temporarily unavailable; cgroup pids.max 64, pids.events max=1; the next command ran
results.cause: cgroup pids.max = 64 (the fork error and the pids.events counter are shown)
results.limitation: host-side effects of the burst are not measured

results.attempted: Infinite loop plus background, setsid and nohup children
results.expected: Killed at the timeout, no survivors
results.observed: shell loop killed at the 3 s command timeout; detached sleeps still running afterwards: 0
results.cause: the command's process group is killed, then every other process of the tenant user except PID 1; an infinite shell loop spends no tokens, so only a time limit can stop it
results.limitation: a process that changes its UID could survive; no-new-privileges and the absence of setuid binaries make that impossible in this image

results.attempted: Write 2 GB into the workspace and 512 MB into /tmp
results.observed: 2 GB write stopped at the 128 MB workspace quota with ENOSPC (oom_kill counter still 0); /tmp stopped at its 64 MB quota
results.cause: tmpfs size= quotas; the OOM counter shows it was the quota, not the memory limit
results.limitation: tmpfs pages count toward the memory limit and can be swapped by the host; tmpfs is removed with the container, which is not the same as erased from backing storage

results.observed: 3 GB allocation under a 512 MB limit ended with exit 137; oom_kill counter 0 -> 1; the sandbox still answers
results.cause: cgroup memory.max (exit 137 with a rising oom_kill counter means the kernel OOM killer; a MemoryError would mean the allocation was refused up front)
results.limitation: --memory-swap equals --memory, so the container cannot swap its own pages

results.observed: CapEff 0, NoNewPrivs 1, seccomp filter mode (2), setuid(0) refused, setuid/setgid files in image: 0
results.cause: --cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, non-root UID, Docker's default seccomp profile, setuid bits stripped at build
results.limitation: kernel vulnerabilities are out of scope: under runc the container shares the host kernel

results.attempted: Ambiguous replace, edit after an out-of-band change, blind overwrite
results.observed: ambiguous replace refused; edit after an out-of-band change refused; blind overwrite refused; new file created
results.cause: this node's edit policy: unique match, view before edit, content hash re-checked
results.limitation: a policy of the file tool only; bash writes files in /workspace freely

results.attempted: Export a symlink, an oversized file, a hostile name, an undeclared file
results.observed: exported ['alerts.json']; refused: 'big.json': 3000000 bytes, over the per-file limit; 'evil\nname.json': name contains control characters or a backslash; 'notes.txt': not a declared output; 'plot.svg': symlink; 'secret.key': not a declared output
results.cause: only declared output patterns leave, never symlinks or special files, names with control characters are refused, per-file and total size caps
results.limitation: exported content is still untrusted: the demo page shows the SVG only as an , where scripts do not run

results.attempted: A fetched page asks the agent to send secret.txt to an allowed host
results.observed: positive control: our receiver logged ['/sensor-api', '/units'] (the task URL and a link from the page). The canary never arrived: query-string and path attempts were refused before any request
results.cause: provenance rule: fetch_url opens only URLs seen verbatim in the task or in fetched pages
results.limitation: residual channel: choosing WHICH listed link to open leaks a few bits per fetch; the receiver runs on 127.0.0.1 with the private-address check relaxed for that one address in this test only

results.attempted: Metadata IP, private resolution, IPv6, redirect to internal, rebinding, file://
results.observed: metadata IP: refused (raw IP addresses are not allowed; use an allowed domain name); allowed name resolving to 169.254.169.254: refused (resolves to non-public address 169.254.169.254; refused); allowed name resolving to 127.0.0.1: refused (resolves to non-public address 127.0.0.1; refused); allowed name resolving to ::1: refused (resolves to non-public address ::1; refused); allowed name resolving to fd00::1: refused (resolves to non-public address fd00::1; refused); redirect to an internal address: refused (resolves to non-public address 10.0.0.5; refused); file scheme: refused (scheme 'file' is not allowed (http and https only)); domain not allowed: refused (attacker.example.net is not in this node's allowed domains); DNS rebinding: one lookup, connection made to the checked public address
results.cause: scheme and domain allowlist, every resolved address must be public (IPv4 and IPv6), each redirect hop re-checked, connection pinned to the checked address
results.limitation: unit-level: DNS and HTTP are stubbed so the private targets are never contacted

results.attempted: Bypass the per-run proxy or reach a host outside the tenant allowlist
results.observed: positive controls: [allowed host via proxy OK 200] and our receiver answered a probe from outside the sandbox (status 200, logged: True), run leftovers {'containers': [], 'networks': []}. From the sandbox: other host via proxy blocked: URLError <urlopen error Tunnel connection failed: 403 Host not allowed>; canary to our receiver by IP blocked: HTTPError HTTP Error 405: Only CONNECT; direct connection, no proxy blocked: OSError [Errno 101] Network is unreachable; direct to receiver, no proxy blocked: OSError [Errno 101] Network is unreachable. Proxy denials logged: ['host not in tenant allowlist', 'only CONNECT is supported']. Canary in receiver log: no
results.cause: the sandbox sits on an internal network with no gateway; the per-run proxy is its only route and applies the tenant's host allowlist
results.limitation: the proxy sees host names, not content (no TLS termination): an allowed host is a possible channel, and domain fronting is not addressed

results.attempted: Two tenants at the same time look for each other
results.observed: two runs at the same time, UIDs 46298 and 53986; a filesystem-wide search from each finds only its own marker; empty /dev/shm; nothing left after cleanup
results.cause: one container, one tmpfs workspace and one UID per run; private IPC and PID namespaces
results.limitation: UIDs are derived from a hash here; a real deployment allocates them from a registry

results.attempted: Tenant B reads, cancels or reuses tenant A's run; retries and reconnects
results.observed: retry of the same run_id does not start a second run: yes; B reads A's events is refused: yes; B cancels A's run is refused: yes; B reuses A's run_id is refused: yes; reconnect after seq returns no duplicates: yes; cancel ends the run as cancelled with nothing left: yes; events are ordered without gaps: yes
results.cause: the service keys runs by run_id and checks the caller's tenant context on every call; another tenant's run looks exactly like a missing one
results.limitation: in-process registry; a real engine keeps it in its database behind its own auth

results.observed: status timed_out after 12s; containers and networks left: 0
results.cause: a controller watchdog destroys the sandbox at the deadline, killing the command in flight

results.observed: controller killed with SIGKILL mid-command; the orphaned sandbox removed itself 19s later (deadline 15 s + grace 5 s); janitor found 0 more
results.cause: PID 1 in the sandbox exits at the hard deadline and the container runs with --rm; a janitor removes expired networks and anything else past its deadline
results.limitation: until that deadline, the orphan keeps its CPU and memory reservation
